chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the young girl who has not yet reached menstruation, he said: 'Her husband divorces her by months.' It was said: 'If he divorces her with one divorce, then a month passes, and then she menstruates in the second month?' He said: 'When she menstruates after he has divorced her for a month, she discards that month and restarts the waiting period with menstruation. If two months pass for her after he divorced her, and then she menstruates in the third, her waiting period is completed by months. When three months have passed for her, she is definitively divorced from him, and he is one of the divisors, and she inherits him and he inherits her as long as she is in the waiting period.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a young girl who has not yet started menstruating?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the transitional legal status of a pre-pubescent girl (*al-jariyah*) upon her first menstruation after divorce, establishing that the waiting period shifts from a fixed three-month duration to a menstrual cycle count. It highlights the scholarly principle that the occurrence of *hayd* retroactively validates the preceding months as part of the *iddah*, thereby confirming her inheritance rights until the third cycle is completed.
